problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨t(6t-4),\,12{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(20,30)$ when $t=2,$ calculate the components of the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$r(t)=⟨${{field-1}}$,\,3{t}^{4}-18\,⟩$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Position Vector Given a Velocity Vector
examples.problem:
The velocity $\mathbf{v}$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
\mathbf{v}(t) = \langle 2t, 3t^2\rangle.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(1,2)$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨2t,3{t}^{2}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 2t\,\text{d}t,\,\int 3{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}+{C}_{1},\,{t}^{3}+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $\mathbf{r} (0)= \langle 1,2 \rangle.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨(0)^{2}+{C}_{1},\,(0)^{3}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,2⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have $C_1=1$ and $C_2=2.$ Therefore, the position vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}+1,\,{t}^{3}+2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
